lots.title: Provision of Fire Risk Assessments
lots.description: London Borough of Bexley Building Services Framework 6278, Lot 1. Supplier to deliver Fire Risk Assessments (FRAs) and associated services across the Council's operational estate, ensuring statutory compliance under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 (as amended by the Fire Safety Act 2021 and s.156 Building Safety Act 2022) and the Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022. Contract period is 2 years with an option to extend for up to a further 12 months (maximum 3 years) commencing April 2026. Scope covers statutory/best-practice FRAs (Type 1-4), Person-Centred FRAs (PCFRA), PAS 9980:2022 Fire Risk Appraisal of External Walls (FRAEW) where applicable, compartmentation survey support, residential building duties under the Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022 (door checks, information boxes, plans, signage, resident information for buildings at 11 m and 18 m thresholds), and risk-based review of emergency lighting (BS EN 1838:2024) and fire detection/alarm systems (BS 5839). Reports must be issued within 10 working days of site completion, integrate with the Council's CAFM system (TF Cloud), include a prioritised action plan, photographic evidence and plan mark-ups, and be produced by individually qualified assessors on the IFE Assessor Register working under a BAFE SP205 (or equivalent UKAS-accredited) certified organisation. The Supplier provides all expertise, staff, labour, materials, equipment and resources; operates under the Council's permits-to-work, dynamic risk assessment, and asbestos management regimes; and supports continuous improvement, environmental and social value objectives.
requirements: Contract term: 2 years with an option to extend for up to 12 months (maximum 3-year term), commencing April 2026.
Provide all expertise, staff, labour, materials, equipment and resources required to deliver Fire Risk Assessments across the Council's operational estate.

Appoint a named representative (Contract Manager) as primary point of contact, responsible for meetings and monthly/quarterly/annual reporting (service performance, asset changes, risks/mitigations, staffing, financial summaries).
Collaborate with the Council's FM team and M&E / building fabric contractors to plan access, coordinate intrusive compartmentation surveys, and maintain site security.

Agree and deliver an annual schedule of FRAs in accordance with Appendix 1 - Bexley Fire Risk Assessment Price Matrix, distinguishing statutory compliance vs best-practice activities, and accommodate schedule changes without additional cost.
Align survey type to risk using the Type 1-4 FRA approach (common parts through to intrusive dwelling inspections) and provide Person-Centred FRAs (PCFRA) for residents requiring support.
Determine and coordinate any required PAS 9980:2022 Fire Risk Appraisal of External Walls (FRAEW) and engage specialist inputs as needed.

Deliver residential-building duties under the Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022: resident information provision, quarterly common-parts and annual flat-door checks, and (for high-rise) information boxes, floor plans, lift checks and wayfinding signage.
Reference BS EN 1838:2024 for emergency lighting and BS 5839 (relevant parts) for fire detection and alarm systems, and align evacuation-lift / EVC strategies with BS 9991:2024.
Propose risk-based review intervals; review FRAs after material changes (occupancy, layout, systems) or fire incidents/near misses.

Issue FRA reports within 10 working days of site completion, covering methodology, scope/limitations, significant findings, persons at risk, preventative/protective measures, aids to evacuation, prioritised action plan with risk rationale, further-investigation flags, photographic evidence and plan mark-ups, in a format compatible with the Council's CAFM system (TF Cloud).
Submit anonymised sample FRAs (one standard and one intrusive) with explanatory notes as part of the tender response.
Individual assessors must hold recognised Fire Risk Assessment qualifications and be listed on the IFE Assessor Register; Associate Membership of IFE alone is not sufficient.
The Supplier organisation must hold BAFE SP205 certification or an equivalent UKAS-accredited scheme and comply with BS ISO 19706:2007 (guidelines for assessing fire threat to people).

Accept work instructions via email and update the Council's CAFM system (TF Cloud) with status and documentation in agreed formats; record completions and upload reports via TF Cloud; submit applications for payment monthly via the system (only completed jobs with required documentation are authorised for payment).
Send all invoices electronically to fmcu.buildingservices@bexley.gov.uk (not Central Payments).

Comply with Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, HSE Guidance Notes and ACOPs, Fire Safety Act 2021, Building Safety Act 2022, Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012, Equality Act 2010 and RIDDOR 2013; submit Risk Assessments and Method Statements (RAMS) for Council approval before commencing work; maintain Workplace Risk Assessments on TF Cloud.
Complete a Dynamic Risk Assessment (DRA) before any planned or reactive works and upload it to TF Cloud (or agreed format); DRA completion is mandatory.

Assume presence of asbestos-containing materials (ACMs) in plant rooms and building fabric unless confirmed otherwise; on discovery/suspicion, cease work, notify the Council, do not disturb ACM without prior written agreement, arrange sampling by qualified firm if instructed, and notify the enforcing authority as required under CAR 2012; operatives must review the Asbestos Risk Management Plan, sign the site asbestos register, and comply with site-specific requirements.

Maintain site security: keep doors/windows closed, switch off lights when not in use, lock up and set alarms on completion, observe the No Smoking policy across all internal and external sites and access routes, and operate formal key handover / key-loss procedures with cost recovery for lost/damaged keys.

Fulfil the duties of the 'Authorised Person' under relevant health and safety legislation for ongoing monitoring, professional oversight and assurance of compliance with all applicable safety and maintenance standards.
Appoint a single Health and Safety point of contact, liaise with the Council's Corporate H&S representative, report all near misses, and comply fully with RIDDOR 2013 reporting obligations.

Provide a clear organisational structure with defined roles, responsibilities and escalation routes; ensure staff competence, continuity of service (cover for sickness/annual leave), DBS checks for all staff and subcontractors, and replacement of removed personnel within 5 working days; all staff must carry valid company ID and sign in/out per site process.

Sub-contracting permitted only with prior Council approval after technical/capability assessment; subcontractors operate under the same terms and DBS regime; Supplier remains fully accountable and must monitor subcontracted technical services via KPIs, spot checks and management oversight.

Operate a formal complaints procedure (submitted with the tender response); report complaints to the Council's FM Client Unit immediately, log and notify the Contract Administrator within 24 hours, remedy service failures within SLA, and submit monthly complaint summaries with year-on-year reduction targets.

Adhere to the Council's Environmental Policy and Social Value priorities; invited to submit Company Environmental Policy with implementation examples and to propose innovations supporting climate resilience, energy efficiency and waste reduction.

Attend monthly operational meetings and quarterly contract performance partnership meetings with the Council (KPIs, H&S compliance, overall performance) and implement agreed continuous improvement measures including digital reporting enhancements (e.g., digital door registers, QR-coded assets, photo-verified remedials).

During mobilisation, agree report templates (including alignment to BS 9792 where applicable), resource plan, programme, KPIs, TF Cloud data fields, and information-exchange protocols (including s.156 FSO record-keeping and information-sharing duties).
